result.explanation: In the Adult Income dataset, 'Married-civ-spouse' is strongly associated with higher income (>50K) compared to 'Never-married'. This is due to socioeconomic and structural factors where married individuals often have greater financial stability, access to joint income, and higher occupational prestige. The model likely learned this correlation during training. Changing marital-status from 'Never-married' to 'Married-civ-spouse' introduces a category with a strong positive association with income, thus increasing the predicted probability of >50K. Removing marital-status (i.e., not applying the feature at all) results in no change, as the model relies on the existing feature value. The original prediction was 0 (≤50K) with 52.21% confidence — removing the feature maintains this, while changing it to 'Married-civ-spouse' shifts the confidence towards >50K, with an estimated 18 to 22 percentage point increase in probability due to the feature's known positive correlation.
